citations.text: OpenEvo comparison of Pillow (2012), Barzilai and Chinn (2018, 2024) and Hanisch and Eirdosh (2023), 2026-11-18. A shared field concept proposed by the comparison; no source defines it.
Pillow, B. H. (2012). Children's discovery of the active mind: Phenomenological awareness, social experience, and knowledge about cognition. Springer.
Barzilai, S., & Chinn, C. A. (2018). On the goals of epistemic education: Promoting apt epistemic performance. Journal of the Learning Sciences, 27(3), 353-389.
Hanisch, S., & Eirdosh, D. (in press). Book on evolutionary anthropology in education, as restated in a claim list (chapters 1, 5, 8, 12, 14, 15); the manuscript was not available to check.

en.general: Other people as a route by which a person comes to know about thinking: talk about mental states, joint work on criteria, and ideas about the mind passed on by a culture. Pillow treats social experience as one of the three kinds of information in his model. Barzilai and Chinn cite him for the point that metacognitive knowledge can be based on social experience. A restatement of the Hanisch and Eirdosh book says it cites work on culturally transmitted ideas about the mind.

examples: A family that often talks about what each person thinks and feels.
A class that agrees a list of criteria for judging a model.
